02 Card Payment Instrument
A Payment Instrument represents the physical or digital form through which a cardholder accesses available credit and performs payment transactions. It enables the cardholder to make purchases, obtain cash advances, and complete other card-based transactions through payment networks and merchant acceptance channels. A payment instrument is typically linked to a credit card account that determines the funding source, credit limit, balances, and repayment obligations. A customer may have multiple payment instruments associated with the same credit card account, such as replacement cards, supplementary cards, virtual cards, tokenised cards, or digital wallet representations.CORE.BRAND

Table NameCORE.CARD_BLOCKED_REASON
Functional NameCard Blocked Reason
Abbreviation
Classification Type Name
Object Type Name
MV Prebuilt
MV Query

DescriptionA Card Block Code identifies the current restriction or status applied to a payment card. Block codes are used to prevent or control card usage for operational, security, fraud, customer service, or lifecycle management reasons. A card may be blocked due to theft, loss, fraud concerns, non-activation, account management activities, or other business events. For example:

Block Code	 Block Code Description
S		 Stolen
(blank/null)		No block — card is active
X		  Lost and replaced / Cancelled
W	 Written off
N		 New card not activated
Y		 Fraud block
P		 Pickup / Confiscate
H		 Hold
J	 	Transfer out
D, A, T, Q, C, etc.	Various	Other system-specific block reasons

Columns Comments
NoColumn NameDescriptionNotes
1PRODUCT_KEYA surrogate key for the Product.
2PRODUCT_BUSINESS_KEYAn encrypted (hash) value of the business key data. This  will be the same value for all data with a common business key. This is called SCD7 by Kimball.

Examples: hash(Customer Id); hash(Country Code).

This is used to simplify look back and get current processing.
6BRAND_BUSINESS_KEYAn encrypted (hash) value of the business key data. This  will be the same value for all data with a common business key. This is called SCD7 by Kimball.

Examples: hash(Customer Id); hash(Country Code).

This is used to simplify look back and get current processing.
7IS_CURRENT_FLAGA flag that indicates this is the current version of the record. Y - Yes; N - No.
8IS_DELETED_FLAGA flag that indicates the record has been deleted in the source system.

Y - Yes, the record has been deleted; 
N - No, the record has not been deleted.
9VALID_FROM_DATETIMEThe date and time on which this record became active.
10VALID_TO_DATETIMEThe date and time on which this record stopped being active.
11BUSINESS_DATA_HASHAn encrypted (hash) of the business data fields for SCD2 processing.
12AUDIT_CREATED_DATETIMEThe date and time on which this record was created.
13AUDIT_LAST_CHANGED_DATETIMEThe date and time on which this record was last changed.

Last Changed Datetime = Created Datetime when the record is first created.
14AUDIT_DATA_PROCESS_KEYThe primary key of the process that created/changed the record.
15AUDIT_CREATED_SOURCEThe source for creating the record. This can be an application, change id and so on.
16AUDIT_LAST_CHANGED_SOURCEThe source for updating the record. This can be an application, change id and so on.

On creation, this will be the same as Audit Create Source.
